eyebrow: Morning Brief · recap of Mon Jun 22 + today's setup
headline: Equities crack, but the plumbing stays calm.
stance: The engine isn't buying the panic: bond-market volatility is near 3-year lows and credit is calm. We stay Risk On · Neutral — this reads as an equity-valuation wobble, not systemic stress.

news.head: Broadcom Q2 miss
news.body: AI-networking revenue $4.1B vs $4.8B expected; the single trigger for Monday's ~$1.4T semiconductor selloff.

news.head: Fed's hawkish turn
news.body: new Chair Kevin Warsh opened hawkish (Jun 17); the dot-plot median now implies a 2026 hike.

news.head: US–Iran framework
news.body: a 60-day roadmap toward a deal; oil fell ~3% Monday, partly recovering overnight.

news.head: Asia chips dragged
news.body: SK Hynix and Samsung each closed −4%+; European tech −3.2%.

implications: The AI-chip trade looks fragile — semis ran ~79% in 100 trading days with no margin for a guidance miss.
A Fed leaning toward hikes against 2.28% real rates is a headwind for high-multiple tech and could begin widening spreads.
A sustained Iran deal adds oil supply within 60 days — structurally bearish energy.
The yen at a 3-year extreme keeps BOJ intervention and carry-unwind risk live.

watch.head: Stress signal (MOVE)
watch.body: a climb toward 116 is the first de-risk line; far off today.

watch.head: Yield regime
watch.body: a push to +33bp flips it inflationary and puts the Fed back in play.

watch.head: Semis
watch.body: stabilize, or does the selling cascade into the cash open?

watch.head: Yen / BOJ
watch.body: any statement with ¥/$ at a 3-year extreme; Iran/oil — framework holds or fractures.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
sections.prose: The 10-year closed at 4.51% (2Y 4.24%, curve +27bp), and the Fed held hawkish at 3.50–3.75% — nine of eighteen officials now see a 2026 hike, with the market eyeing October. Real rates are restrictive at 2.28% while breakeven inflation (2.23%) stays contained. The yen closed at 161.6, its weakest in three years.
sections.positioning: Rate-futures speculators have almost no bullish bets left — a contrarian floor; much of the hike fear may already be priced.

sections.title: Equity Markets
sections.prose: The S&P 500 closed Monday at 7,472.79; overnight futures are −1.4%, pointing to a sharply lower open (Nasdaq 100 closed 26,166.60). The drop followed Broadcom's 14% AI-chip revenue miss, which erased ~$1.4T of value — the Philadelphia Semi Index fell 10% on the session, Marvell −17%. VIX closed at 17.3, still moderate, but with CAPE at 41.6 valuations leave little room.
sections.positioning: Small-cap (Russell 2000) speculators are nearly out of bullish bets — a contrarian floor; small caps may hold up better than large-cap tech.

single_name.note: (Taiwan Semiconductor) — insiders buying; the core AI picks-and-shovels name, cheaper after the rout.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
sections.prose: Credit isn't corroborating the equity stress. IG spreads closed at 74bp and high-yield at 266bp over — near three-year tights — with bank reserves ample at $3.03T and funding flat to policy. No distress is leaking from the selloff.
sections.positioning: High-yield dealers are piled into inventory near a 3-year peak — a contrarian warning; thinner cushion if selling accelerates.

single_name.note: (Radian, a mortgage insurer) — insiders buying; a stable-credit, housing-levered play.
